name: ComfyUI
what: A node-graph front end and server for image and video models. It holds its models on the card between jobs, which is why a dashboard that manages one card needs to know about it.

detect.venv: venv or .venv inside or beside the checkout; the one a running ComfyUI uses wins, else the one with the accelerators (sage attention, triton, xformers)

can: start it with the recorded argv
stop only a process on its port whose command line names ComfyUI
ask it to drop its models
read how much of the card it holds from the operating system
run queued image batches between resident models (the art queue)
cannot: read workflows, the queue's contents or outputs
run with --listen: it has no login

update.note: The ComfyUI procedure: fast-forward to the newest vX.Y.Z tag, reinstall requirements with torch, torchvision, torchaudio (and triton-windows) pinned at their installed versions, boot test on cuda, roll back by itself if it does not boot. Custom nodes are not updated.

all: python -m venv venv; install the torch build that matches your CUDA from pytorch.org, then venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt
Models go under models/ by type; the art queue names them in the inventory's art.models.

good: image and video generation with full control of the graph
sharing a card with a resident model, when the dashboard parks one for the other
not: a service that stays reachable beyond the machine: put a login in front first
